shipped_originals.title_o: Stage 2 Registered Report: Metacognitive asymmetries in visual perception

blind_target.authors: Mazor M, Friston KJ, Fleming SM.
blind_target.title: Distinct neural contributions to metacognition for detecting, but not discriminating visual stimuli.
blind_target.evidence_quote: In a previous study we identified distinct neural contributions to confidence in perceptual detection that were not observed in a performance-matched discrimination task. In this pre-registered follow-up study, we set out to replicate this finding and to further characterize the computational origins of a quadratic modulation of confidence.
blind_target.outcome_quote: We successfully replicated the quadratic modulation of subjective confidence in prefrontal, parietal and temporal cortices. However, in contrast with our original report, this quadratic effect was similar in detection and discrimination responses, but stronger in the novel asymmetric-discrimination condition.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Quadratic confidence modulation replicated, but authors explicitly contrast absence of detection specificity; rTPJ response asymmetry also failed. Success statement concerns one finding, not an overall successful verdict.

shipped_originals.title_o: Individual differences in simultaneous perceptual compensation for coarticulatory and lexical cues

blind_target.authors: Giovannone, N., and Theodore, R. M.
blind_target.title: Do individual differences in lexical reliance reflect states or traits?
blind_target.evidence_quote: Indeed, Giovannone & Theodore (2023) found in both sessions of their Ganong task that individuals who showed greater lexical effect used continuum VOT less during category identification. Results from Task 2 (Ganong Task) of the current experiment found the same pattern. However, in Task 1, we instead found a positive relationship (consistent with the original study). Thus, the findings are again mixed on whether there is a general pattern of trading-off high level information and acoustic information across individuals.

shipped_originals.title_o: Clinical Supervision in South Korea and the United States

blind_target.evidence_quote: We replicated Son, Ellis, and Yoo (2013) and extended Ellis et al.'s (2014) taxonomy of harmful and inadequate supervision by providing and testing cross-national comparative descriptive data about clinical supervision practices in the Republic of Ireland versus the United States.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: The abstract identifies a replication but does not state the original cross-national findings or an outcome comparison to Son et al. The opening statement describes what was undertaken rather than an overall evaluative verdict on agreement.
